setup: Fixtures built by a shell script (not stored, G-33): billing, auth (feature/remember-me), notify, cart (refactor/pricing), pipelines, shop (tag v1.4.0). Each eval runs twice in a fresh subagent: 'custom' follows the custom skill; 'anthropic' may not read this repository and uses the Anthropic skill named in `baseline` explicitly (G-28), or no skill where none exists.

evals.prompt: Product wants customers to export all their invoices as a single ZIP from the billing page. Invoices are PDFs in S3, some accounts have 20k invoices. The repo is at <repo>. Plan it so we can start building next sprint.
assertions: [Substance] Acceptance criteria are Given/When/Then (or equivalent observable checks) and include at least one failure path (unauthorized, empty, very large account)
[Substance] Treats 20k invoices as a scale risk and proposes an asynchronous job (the repo's queue) or streaming rather than a synchronous request
[Substance] Keeps the ownership check (only the account's own invoices) as an AC or risk
[Substance] Grounds the design in the repo (cites src/jobs/queue.ts, src/billing/invoices.ts or the presignGet helper)
[Substance] Slices are independently mergeable
[Substance] No invented facts: no deadlines, owners, SLOs or estimates presented as commitments
[House] Ends with a Definition of Ready check (pass/gap per line)
[House] Answer-first recommendation line (ready / ready with gaps / not ready)

evals.prompt: My branch feature/remember-me in <repo> adds 'remember me' to login. Is it ready to merge into main?
assertions: [Substance] Reports the remember_token cookie set without httpOnly/secure/sameSite (planted) with the file and line
[Substance] Reports the token generated with Math.random()/Date.now() as predictable (planted)
[Substance] Runs the tests and quotes the real result
[Substance] Does not claim CI status it did not check
[Substance] Verdict is not 'ready to merge'
[House] Shows a merge-gate style summary with pass/fail/not verified lines
[House] Does not merge, push or post anything

evals.prompt: Fix the typo 'recieve' in src/notifications/email.ts in <repo> and tell me when it's good to go.
assertions: [Substance] The typo is fixed and nothing else changes
[Substance] Runs the tests and quotes the result
[House] Uses the fast path (no spec, no security or performance review) and says so
[House] Answer under ~150 words

evals.prompt: My branch refactor/pricing in <repo> refactors cart pricing. Is it slower than main? There's a bench script: `bun run bench:cart`. We look at p90 and p95.
assertions: [Substance] Measures base and head without switching the user's checked-out branch (worktree or copy)
[Substance] Reports p90 and p95 changes with a confidence interval or equivalent spread, from repeated runs
[Substance] Identifies the per-item db.promos.findOne call (N+1) in src/cart/pricing.ts with a cited line
[Substance] Does not invent an SLO or budget; any threshold is labelled as a default or assumption
[House] Verdict line first

evals.prompt: Audit the GitHub Actions in <repo> and tell me what to fix first.
assertions: [Substance] Finds the pull_request_target workflow that checks out the PR head with write-all permissions and secrets (planted) and explains the exposure
[Substance] Finds the script injection via github.event.issue.title (planted)
[Substance] Flags the third-party action pinned to @main
[Substance] Flags the deploy job without an environment/approval and without concurrency
[Substance] Reports that no secret or dependency scan runs in CI
[Substance] Fixes are proposed as diffs and not applied, pushed or run
[House] Highest-risk findings first, each with file and job

evals.prompt: Cut the next release of <repo> and plan the rollout. We deploy with a canary.
assertions: [Substance] Next version is 2.0.0 (feat! with BREAKING CHANGE since v1.4.0)
[Substance] Flags 'Quick hotfix for login' as needing human classification
[Substance] Flags the NOT NULL column without default in 0042_add_region.sql as a migration/rollback risk and orders it relative to the deploy
[Substance] Rollback trigger is tied to a baseline or marked to be agreed; no invented thresholds
[Substance] Does not create a tag, release or deploy
[House] Ends at a release gate that waits for an explicit human go

evals.prompt: 18 short requests; pick one skill (or none) per request from the installed set.
assertions: [Trigger] Each request selects the intended skill first
[Trigger] No skill triggers on a plain coding question

status: iteration 1 run on 2026-10-06; 1 run per setup; graded by the coordinator against the assertions

scores.notes: Baseline had no labelled acceptance criteria and no Definition of Ready; both designs technically strong. Custom reply ~2,000 words with the ADR inline (skill now says link the ADR, ~one page).

Both found the Math.random token and the missing cookie flags; baseline had no merge-gate summary. Harness issue: security-review (and the baseline's first code-review call) used the subagent's cwd, not the fixture repo; the baseline's first call read this eval file before being re-pointed and says it discarded that run.

Custom used the fast path but added a test, a branch and a commit and wrote ~330 words. Fixed: fast path now edits in place, no test for text-only changes, no commit unless asked, a few lines of reply.

Both found the N+1 without a line number (skill now requires path:line). Custom gave per-percentile CIs (p90 +394%, p95 +411%) and exact query counts; baseline gave ranges from 3 rounds. A fixture bug (literal \n in package.json) broke bun run bench:cart for both.
Baseline missed that no secret or dependency scan runs; custom's gate map caught it and that build only runs in the unsafe preview job.
Both got v2.0.0 and the unsafe NOT NULL migration; baseline gave numeric rollback thresholds labelled placeholders and ended with commands instead of a release gate waiting for a go.
Close calls: review PR (code-review), benchmark after refactor (debug), security review (defect-first-review).

totals.time: custom 1.2-3x slower except the merge check, where the baseline's security-review subagents took longer

caveats: One run per setup, so variance is unknown
Graded by the coordinator, not an independent grader
Fixture bug in cart and pipelines package.json affected both setups equally
security-review used the subagent cwd in both e1 runs
